CRM.rationale: CRM presents a compelling but conditional investment case. The franchise is genuinely dominant — #1 CRM vendor for 13 consecutive years with 20% global market share, 150K+ customers, ~90% Fortune 500 penetration, and $67.9B RPO providing strong forward visibility. Revenue accelerated to +13.3% YoY ($11.13B Q1 FY2027), EPS grew +52.2% YoY to $2.42, and net margin expanded to 18.7% (pack ratio) from 12.7% prior regime. Agentforce ARR hit $1.2B (+205% YoY) with a $1.6B VA contract validating federal demand. The trailing PE at 19.6x is 64% below its 12-month average of ~50-55x, and the 5.1% earnings yield now exceeds the 4.68% 10Y Treasury — a historically unusual condition for this name. However, the balance sheet has been radically transformed: debt quadrupled from $8.44B to $39.28B while equity halved from $61.33B to $34.23B, consistent with a large leveraged acquisition (likely Informatica). The margin expansion that drives the low PE may partly reflect acquisition accounting rather than pure operating leverage — the ROE surge from 7.9% to 23.4% is mechanically inflated by the equity decline. The trailing-vs-forward PE gap (19.6x vs ~13x forward) implies consensus expects ~50% earnings growth, which is aggressive. Risks include AI cannibalization of seat-based revenue, Tableau/Commerce Cloud softness flagged by Evercore ISI, and security concerns from ShinyHunters breach claims. The near-term catalyst is Q2 FY2027 earnings (~Sep 2026) where Salesforce has beaten estimates four consecutive quarters, and continued Agentforce deal momentum could re-rate the stock. Score reflects strong franchise quality and historically cheap valuation, tempered by balance-sheet risk and uncertainty about margin sustainability.
